LLM agents¶

An LLM agent is a loop around a model: it reads the task, decides whether to call a tool, reads what came back, and decides again. The loop ends when the model answers without asking for a tool, or when the step budget runs out. Everything else in this framework exists to make that loop observable and to give it tools worth calling.

Defining one¶

An agent needs a model, a set of tools and an instruction. Nothing else is required, and the defaults are chosen so that a first agent is four lines long rather than forty.

from adk import Agent, tool

@tool
def lookup(city: str) -> str:
    """Return the current weather for a city."""
    return fetch_weather(city)

agent = Agent(model="gemini-2.0-flash", tools=[lookup],
              instruction="Answer weather questions. Call lookup for facts.")

What the loop guarantees

  • Every tool call is recorded before it runs.
    • Arguments are validated against the tool signature.
    • A failure is returned to the model, not raised to the caller.
  • The step budget is a hard stop, not a suggestion.

Parameters

NameDefaultWhat it does
max_steps12Hard stop on loop iterations.
temperature0.2Passed straight to the model.

Workflow agents compose several of these; see workflow agents for the sequential and parallel forms. The protocol itself is described in the agent protocol specification, which is maintained outside this project.
